correctness.rationale: For 0<alpha≤gamma≤1, alpha*y0<1 ensures x stays positive and the predator multiplier 1−gamma+alpha*x/(1+x) lies strictly in (0,1). An upper x bound x0+rn makes sum 1/(1+x_j) divergent at alpha=gamma, proving y→0; subcritical alpha<gamma gives geometric decrease. The proof's barrier argument yields x_n→∞ and scalar comparison to the monotone large-x prey-only map gives x=O(log n). The predator decrement is then superpolynomially smaller than re*x*exp(−x); the integral time change G(x)=∫exp(t)/(re*t)dt has increments 1+o(1) and G(x_n)~n, proving x_n=log n+loglog n+log(re)+o(1). Cesaro averaging yields subcritical log-multiplier rate; expansion of log(1−gamma/(1+x_n)) gives critical −gamma*n/log n. All are for invariant initial region; 100000-step experiments only corroborated slow convergence.
